newsitem.title: USA: U.S. MTBE FIRMS ON TALK OF PDVSA FORCE MAJEURE.
newsitem.headline: U.S. MTBE FIRMS ON TALK OF PDVSA FORCE MAJEURE.

text.p: U.S. spot MTBE prices rose in moderate activity on Wednesday, with New York Harbor up on talk Venezuela declared force majeure on four reformulated gasoline cargoes.
Venezuela's state-owned oil campany declared the force majure on all the output from its fire-stricken Curacao oil refinery in the Caribbean.
The company said no shipments had yet been cancelled but U.S. and Venezuela traders have said four RFG cargoes have so far been annulled.
One major player has confirmed that a 260,000 to 300,000 barrel cargo it was to have received from Venezuela for the Harbor had been annulled.
In the U.S. Gulf, prompt MTBE was done at 94.75 cents for 50,000 barrels, with the range at 94.50/95.00 cents, about a half cent above Tuesday.
New York Harbor also rose, about 1.50 cents to 101.00/102.00 cents, largely on news of the force majeure and the wide spread between RFG and conventional.
-- Laney Salisbury, New York Energy Desk +1 212 859 1631--
